stem:
A psychiatrist reviews a 23-year-old who has been well for four months after a first episode of schizophrenia. Oral aripiprazole is effective and well tolerated; he is back at university and has stopped cannabis. He asks to stop medication because he feels recovered, but is willing to discuss relapse prevention.

Which plan is most appropriate at this review?

options.label: A
options.text: Taper aripiprazole now because functioning has recovered
options.explanation: Functional recovery is encouraging, but four months of remission is early for withdrawal after a first psychotic episode. Stopping now carries substantial relapse risk.

options.label: B
options.text: Halve the dose now and complete withdrawal at six months of remission
options.explanation: Planning complete withdrawal after only six months still falls within the period of high early relapse risk. His effective, well-tolerated treatment should continue with later individual review of withdrawal.

options.label: C
options.text: Continue aripiprazole; review withdrawal later in recovery
options.explanation: Discuss the high early relapse risk and agree on continued treatment with regular review. Later withdrawal can be considered individually after sustained recovery rather than treating medication as automatically lifelong.

options.label: D
options.text: Change to a depot preparation before considering his request
options.explanation: A depot may suit someone who prefers it or has difficulty with daily dosing. Neither indication is described here, and changing formulation does not answer his question about duration.

options.label: E
options.text: Commit to the current dose indefinitely after this first episode
options.explanation: Long-term treatment may become appropriate, but an unconditional lifelong commitment is not justified solely by one episode. Benefits, harms and preferences need continuing review.

context: Early remission after a first psychotic episode does not remove the need for relapse-prevention treatment.
